¶ 32. Abortions] Lifeless foetuses soon to be stillborn, as ll. 9–10 make clear.
 death-white] Both the Harvard holographs read thus; death- is careted in above the line in Harvard
Nbk 1.1839 and Athenaeum 1832 read white, as do the drafts in Nbk 14 and Mary Copybk 1.
 with which she travaileth] with which she is in labour.
 redressor] ‘One who redresses or rectifies (esp. a wrong)’: OED.
 festival] festal Athenaeum 1832.
 crying havoc!] To ‘cry havoc’ was originally the signal to an army to despoil and pillage a conquered
enemy (OED havoc n. 1) as in Julius Caesar III i 276.
 that] which Harvard Nbk 1, Mary Copybk 1, Athenaeum 1832, 1839. Bacchanal triumph] The
phrase associates two kinds of ceremony practised in ancient Rome. A triumph was a formal proces-
sion commemorating a military victory over a foreign foe (see MA 57 and note). The celebration of
the Bacchanalia involved secret religious rites in honour of Bacchus (Gk Dionysus), the god of wine
